how_it_works: An agency-editorial treatment (Obys Agency lineage: USSR Design Almanac, VENUS, the 2026 Obys.com rebuild) where the ROLE TITLE itself becomes the hero object of each Experience beat: an oversized display headline (think 12-30vw / 120-360px) that scrubs, scales, and re-composes on scroll, surrounded by deliberate silence and only a few lines of body copy. The interaction model is scroll-as-playhead but the animated subject is TYPE, not cards: as you scroll into a beat, the giant role title enters/settles (mask-reveal from a clip, or scale from ~0.9->1 with a slight y drift), holds while sparse supporting copy (org, dates, 1-2 outcome lines) fades in beneath or beside it, then the next role's oversized title takes over as the previous scales/blurs away. Obys builds this with a custom rAF + Web Animations API engine and Lenis-style virtual scroll; the transferable GSAP recipe is a ScrollTrigger with CSS `position: sticky` (NOT `pin`) on the type stage, one timeline, `scrub: 0.3-1`, and `gsap.set` inside `onUpdate` mapping `self.progress` to `scale`/`opacity`/`y` on the headline (per the Codrops 'Building Horeca' performance write-up: scale via transform only, sticky over pin, scrub 0.3 ≈ scrub 0.1 visually but far cheaper). Editorially it works like a magazine spread sequence: dense 'statement' moments (the giant title) alternate with calm readable blocks (the actual resume content) — 'tension and silence between strong statements,' as Obys describes their own storytelling. What moves: the role title (scale/mask/scrub), maybe an oversized ghost year in the background at a slower parallax rate. What stays: a persistent section label / progress marker and the readable body block once revealed. Critical constraint for a resume: each beat should consume ~1 viewport of scroll (not a multi-thousand-px pin per role) so 5 beats don't turn into a 6000px+ scroll-jail — cap the takeover to the CURRENT/marquee role(s) and let the rest scan normally.
visual_structure: One beat = a near-full-viewport editorial 'spread' anchored by the role title set enormous. Layout of a single beat: (1) the ROLE as an oversized Fraunces display line — the visual event of the section (e.g. 'ML Engineer' or 'Clinical Data Scientist' filling most of the width); (2) a small mono/label date range as an overline or corner tag ('2026 — PRESENT'); (3) the org/company as a quiet secondary line (Inter), often baseline-aligned to the giant title or tucked in a lower corner; (4) 1-2 short outcome lines MAX as sparse body copy (each <= 2 lines; the whole point of the style is scarcity of prose — Obys uses 'silence between statements'); (5) one restrained proof chip / metric in maroon. Because the title is the composition, the rest is arranged around its negative space — copy in a corner, dates opposite, generous whitespace on paper (#FAF9F6). Beats do NOT stack as visible cards; they succeed each other in the same sticky stage and MORPH: the outgoing giant title scales down + fades/blurs while the incoming one scales up into place, so the section reads as a sequence of full-bleed type spreads. A faint oversized background year or an accent hairline can add depth. Legibility law: exactly one role title is dominant at any scroll position, and the small body copy for the active beat must be fully readable at rest (16-18px Inter, line-height ~1.5), never left mid-transition.
motion_recipe: GSAP + CSS sticky, transforms only. Structure: `gsap.matchMedia()` gating the takeover to `(min-width: 768px)` and `(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Stage the type in a `position: sticky; top: 0` container (sticky beats GSAP `pin` here — no pin-spacer / stacking-context / mobile address-bar-resize bugs, per Codrops Horeca). One `ScrollTrigger` per beat (or one master timeline): `start: 'top top'`, `end: '+=<~100vh per beat>'`, `scrub: 0.3-0.8` (never `scrub: true` — wheel/trackpad ticks judder on large text; 0.3 looks identical to 0.1 but costs far less CPU). Drive the headline with `gsap.set` in `onUpdate`: `scale` (e.g. 0.92 -> 1 -> 1.06 as it exits), `opacity`, small `y` (24-40px), optional `filter: blur(6px)->0->blur(6px)`. Reveal the title via a mask/clip (`clip-path` inset or a wrapper `overflow:hidden` + inner translate) rather than per-letter splitting. Body copy: simple fade + 16px rise, once (`toggleActions: 'play none none reverse'`), staggered ~80ms after the title lands. Add `force3D: true` / `will-change: transform` on the active title only. Init inside `document.fonts.ready.then(() => { init(); ScrollTrigger.refresh(); })` because Fraunces/Inter font-swap shifts trigger positions; set `ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true })`; clean up with `useGSAP({ scope })` / `gsap.context()`. Use fluid sizing: `font-size: clamp(3rem, 14vw, 22rem); line-height: 0.95` so the giant title never forces horizontal scroll on mobile. WHAT NOT TO ANIMATE: never animate `font-size`/layout props (animate `transform: scale` instead — font-size triggers layout every frame and 'breaks screen-reader focus'); do not per-letter-split the title with SplitText/`<span>` per character (Adrian Roselli / Unicorn Club: screen readers read it letter-by-letter; if you must split, keep one accessible text node via `aria-label` + `aria-hidden` on the pieces); no infinite marquee/shimmer on the title; don't animate body-copy tracking/line-height; don't scrub the actual reading content, only the display title. Keep total motion per beat under ~a few seconds of scroll and honor WCAG 2.2.2 (a way to stop/skip).
reduced_motion: Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (and gated so the whole takeover only mounts on `no-preference` via `gsap.matchMedia`), drop the sticky stage, the scrub, and the scale entirely. Render each beat as a static editorial block: the role title STILL set large (the oversized type is layout/brand, not motion, so keep it — just cap it a touch smaller and let it sit still), with its date overline, org, sparse copy, and maroon proof chip all visible in document flow, stacked reverse-chronologically. No pin, no scrub, no blur, no count-up. Transitions collapse to instant or a single <=150ms opacity fade on enter. This static, all-content-visible stack doubles as (a) the a11y path, (b) the mobile fallback, and (c) the fast-scan recruiter path and print/ATS baseline. Crucially, because the DOM already holds each title as a normal readable text node (no per-letter split), the content is fully exposed to screen readers whether or not motion plays — the two concerns (motion preference vs. DOM readability) are handled independently.
brand_fit: MEDIUM (HIGH only if scoped to ONE marquee beat; LOW if applied to all 5 roles). Reason: The Obys editorial-type ethos — graphic-design discipline, strong typography, grid, 'tension and silence between statements' — is genuinely aligned with Madhavi's editorial-minimal, Fraunces + Inter, maroon-on-paper (#8B2E2A / #FAF9F6) system, and it is emphatically NOT purple-SaaS slop, so aesthetically it fits the brand thesis. It can make the CURRENT role feel like a confident magazine cover and signal design maturity. BUT there is a hard tension with the audience: hiring managers/recruiters scan a portfolio in ~3-10 seconds (often ~1 minute total, frequently on mobile) in an F-pattern, and the oversized-type takeover trades information density for spectacle — an entire viewport spent on one word ('Engineer') is the opposite of a scannable reverse-chronological list. Applied to all five beats (nference FT, nference intern, AMC clinical, DEXTER ML, Animations Media) it becomes a long, prose-starved scroll spectacle where dates and outcomes — the things a recruiter actually needs — are buried under decoration, and it risks reading as 'agency demo reel' rather than 'clinical-AI credibility.' There are also real a11y traps (per-letter SplitText breaking screen readers, animated font-size breaking SR focus) that must be actively avoided. Verdict: steal the oversized-title AS A HERO/section-opener device for the one signature role, keep every other beat as a scannable list, and always ship the static reduced-motion fallback. Scoped that way it's HIGH; as a full-experience treatment it's a delight-over-utility trap for this audience.
steal: Steal the oversized role title as a single editorial ANCHOR for the marquee (current) beat only: set the current role in Fraunces at `clamp(3rem, 14vw, 18rem)`, line-height ~0.95, on paper, with just a mono date overline, the org line, ONE outcome sentence, and a maroon proof chip arranged in its negative space — then let it mask/scale-reveal once (or scrub gently) as the Experience section opens. It borrows Obys's 'strong typographic statement + silence' to give the Experience block a confident, non-generic entry point and a clear focal role, WITHOUT converting the whole career into a scroll spectacle. Everything after that opener reverts to a scannable reverse-chronological list. This captures the editorial wow at the section header while keeping the section skimmable and mobile-safe.
avoid: Avoid turning every role into a full-viewport oversized-type spread (the literal Obys takeover for all 5 beats). Three concrete failure modes: (1) Recruiter friction — spending a whole screen on one giant word starves the beat of the dates/outcomes recruiters skim for, forces linear scroll through a spectacle, and reads as agency show-reel over clinical credibility; keep prose sparse but keep the SCANNABLE FACTS present and above the fold per beat. (2) Accessibility — do NOT per-letter-split the giant titles (GSAP SplitText / `<span>`-per-char) for the scrub effect: screen readers announce it letter-by-letter (documented by Adrian Roselli and Unicorn Club, 2026); keep one real text node and, if splitting for visuals, use `aria-label` + `aria-hidden` on the fragments. Never animate `font-size` (animate `transform: scale`) because size changes 'break screen-reader focus' and thrash layout. (3) Performance/scroll-jail — don't `pin` a multi-thousand-px stage per role (use CSS sticky, scrub 0.3, ~1 viewport per beat, `clamp()` sizing so titles never cause horizontal scroll on mobile), and always provide a WCAG 2.2.2 stop/skip + a static reduced-motion fallback that exposes all content.
